page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 64 vCPUs and 240 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance features 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in two threads per core. The processor architecture includes a 45 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache. It supports hardware-level features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and Bit Manipulation Instruction Set 2 (BMI2), though it lacks AVX-512 support. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities alongside weak single-core execution. In single-core tests, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded gzip compression, the instance scores in the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core place the instance in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also register average performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 74.56 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 29.73 GB/sec.

The resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU positions this instance for balanced workloads that scale horizontally across many threads rather than relying on high single-thread performance. It achieves average throughput in database operations, Redis SET operations (40.61 million operations per second), and static web serving (24.4 GB/sec). Large language model inference benchmarks show average prompt processing speeds but weak text generation speeds. This profile suggests the instance is suited for multi-threaded general-purpose applications, web serving, and moderate database workloads, offering a standard resource allocation without the premium cost of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware.

The hardware configuration lacks bundled GPUs and local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff: single-core execution is weak, placing in the bottom 25% for tasks like single-threaded compression and Geekbench single-core tests. However, the instance delivers average multi-core performance and memory bandwidth, scoring in the middle 50% for multi-threaded decompression, PassMark CPU, and Redis SET operations. With a balanced allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from parallel processing rather than high single-thread clock speeds.
